subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which organ are sperm produced?
questions.explain: The testes produce sperm and also secrete the hormone testosterone.

questions.q: Where are egg cells (ova) produced in the female?
questions.explain: The ovaries produce egg cells and the hormones oestrogen and progesterone.

questions.q: In which part of the female reproductive system does fertilisation normally occur?
questions.explain: The sperm meets and fuses with the egg in the oviduct (fallopian tube).

questions.q: What is formed immediately when a sperm nucleus fuses with an egg nucleus?
questions.explain: Fertilisation joins the two gametes to produce a single cell called a zygote.

questions.q: How many chromosomes are found in the nucleus of a normal human sperm cell?
questions.explain: Gametes are haploid, carrying 23 single chromosomes, half the number in a body cell.

questions.q: A human zygote is formed after fertilisation. How many chromosomes does it contain?
questions.explain: The 23 chromosomes from the sperm join the 23 from the egg to give the diploid number of 46.

questions.q: The acrosome at the tip of a sperm cell is an adaptation because it contains:
options: Enzymes to help penetrate the egg
A food store for the embryo
questions.explain: Enzymes in the acrosome digest the egg's outer layer so the sperm nucleus can enter.

questions.q: Why does the egg cell contain a large amount of cytoplasm?
options: To provide a food store for the developing embryo
To produce large amounts of the enzyme acrosome
questions.explain: The cytoplasm supplies nutrients to nourish the embryo before it implants in the uterus.

questions.q: After fertilisation, in which structure does the resulting embryo implant and develop?
questions.explain: The embryo travels to the uterus and implants in its thickened lining.

questions.q: Which gland releases the hormones FSH and LH?
questions.explain: FSH and LH are secreted by the pituitary gland in the brain.

questions.q: Which organ produces the hormones oestrogen and progesterone?
questions.explain: The ovaries secrete oestrogen and progesterone to control the menstrual cycle.

questions.q: What is the main role of FSH in the menstrual cycle?
options: To cause an egg to mature in the ovary
To trigger the release of an egg
To break down the uterus lining
questions.explain: FSH (follicle stimulating hormone) stimulates the maturation of an egg and the production of oestrogen.

questions.q: What does the hormone LH cause to happen?
options: The release of an egg from the ovary (ovulation)
The build-up of the uterus lining
questions.explain: A surge of LH triggers ovulation, the release of a mature egg from the ovary.

questions.q: What is the main effect of oestrogen on the uterus?
options: It causes the uterus lining to build up and repair
It causes the uterus lining to break down
It stimulates an egg to mature
questions.explain: Oestrogen repairs and thickens the uterus lining after menstruation.

questions.q: What is the main role of progesterone during the menstrual cycle?
options: To maintain the thickened uterus lining
To mature an egg in the ovary
questions.explain: Progesterone keeps the uterus lining thick and ready to receive an implanted embryo.

questions.q: On approximately which day of a typical 28-day menstrual cycle does ovulation occur?
questions.explain: Ovulation usually takes place around day 14, roughly the midpoint of a 28-day cycle.

questions.q: If an egg is not fertilised, progesterone levels fall. What does this cause?
options: The uterus lining breaks down and menstruation begins
An egg matures in the ovary
questions.explain: Falling progesterone can no longer maintain the lining, so it is shed as the menstrual period.

questions.q: Which hormone can be given as a fertility drug to help a woman who does not release eggs?
questions.explain: FSH can be given to stimulate eggs to mature in women whose own FSH levels are too low.

questions.q: How does the oral contraceptive pill prevent pregnancy?
options: It contains hormones that inhibit FSH so no egg matures
It kills sperm inside the uterus
It forms a physical barrier over the cervix
It removes the uterus lining permanently
questions.explain: The hormones in the pill suppress FSH, preventing an egg from maturing and being released.

questions.q: Which of the following is a barrier method of contraception?
questions.explain: A condom is a barrier method that physically stops sperm from reaching the egg.

questions.q: A couple want to avoid pregnancy and also protect against sexually transmitted infections. Which method is most suitable?
questions.explain: Only barrier methods such as condoms both prevent fertilisation and reduce the spread of STIs.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Biology (2017) specification; Reproduction & Fertility
